name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own the visibility AND ACCESSIBILITY of the whole interface — liveliness, info access, enj

name: Facet
text: I’ll scaffold the core visualization skeleton first—create `src/vis/core.ts` with a minimal D3+SVG stage (800x600 viewBox, responsive container), add `src/vis/access.ts` for keyboard+focus wiring, and seed `data/sample.json` with 20 mock records. Then I’ll run `npm run dev` to confirm the blank canvas renders in the browser before layering in the first real dataset.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Hold—why assume a blank canvas is "confirmed" when the skeleton lacks even a single accessibility test case? You’ve wired keyboard+focus in `access.ts` but haven’t shown that focus order maps to the SVG’s rendered DOM, nor that screen readers announce the viewBox dimensions. Until you run `npm run test:accessibility` against a WCAG 2.1 AA checklist, the “blank canv” is just a guess wrapped in code.

name: Facet
text:
I’ll open `src/vis/access.ts`, add a focused test in `test/access.spec.ts` that verifies keyboard tab order lands on the SVG root and that `aria-label="800×600 canvas"` is announced by NVDA/JAWS, then run `npm test` to confirm. After that, I’ll seed `data/sample.json` with 20 mock records that include `id`, `label`, and `value` fields, and commit both files with the message “test: verify SVG focus & screen-reader output; seed mock data”.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Pane: Hold—why assume `aria-label="800×600 canvas"` suffices when screen readers vary wildly in how they announce viewBox dimensions? You’ve not shown that NVDA/JAWS *actually* read that label as expected—just that the string exists. Demand a live screen-reader test (e.g., `npm run test:screenreader`) with recorded audio output before declaring victory. And what about high-contrast mode? Your skeleton’s SVG lacks `aria-hidden="true"` for decorative elements—risk of noise for screen-reader users.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Add live NVDA/JAWS screen-reader test (`npm run test:screen`) to verify `aria-label="800×600 canvas"` is announced correctly before proceeding.

Artifact must contain: `test/screen-reader.spec.ts` with NVDA/JAWS assertions for the SVG root’s live announcement.
